name: AR-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strongly Republican district (R+13 PVI) with incumbent Steve Womack renominated
Womack's massive financial advantage ($2.4M cash vs. ~$6K for Ryerse)
No polling and no expert ratings; fundamentals and markets point heavily Republican
Polymarket prices Democratic win at just 6%
model.rationale: The baseline (-15.6) already reflects a strong GOP lean, incumbency, and money edge; the only evidence beyond it—Womack's overwhelming fundraising lead and prediction-market pricing—confirms rather than contradicts it, so I shade slightly more Republican within the allowed range.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic spending or a major scandal involving Womack could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Arkansas's third district is firmly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about thirteen points toward the GOP. Steve Womack, the longtime incumbent, was renominated without difficulty and enters the general election with a dominant financial position: roughly $2.4 million on hand after raising nearly $1.9 million. His Democratic opponent, Robb Ryerse, has raised about $120,000 and had under $6,000 in cash as of the latest filing, leaving little capacity to communicate with voters.

There are no public general-election polls and no expert ratings for this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give Womack about a 95 percent chance of winning. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot, which may siphon a few votes but is unlikely to change the outcome. Everything points to a comfortable Republican hold.
